a: The Amalekites

q: Why did God say the Amalekites would be punished?
a: They attacked tired Israel and did not fear God

q: According to Deuteronomy 25, which people did the Amalekites attack on Israel's journey from Egypt, when Israel was tired and weary?
a: All the stragglers

q: In Deuteronomy 26, what were the Israelites to put in a basket and bring to the place the LORD would choose after entering the land?
a: Some of the firstfruits of all their produce from the soil

q: In Deuteronomy 26, to whom was the Israelite to bring the basket of firstfruits and declare that he had entered the land?
a: The priest serving at that time

q: In Deuteronomy 26, where did the priest place the basket of firstfruits after taking it from the worshiper's hands?
a: Before the altar of the LORD your God

q: In the declaration of Deuteronomy 26, how does the worshiper describe his father?
a: “A wandering Aramean”

q: In Deuteronomy 26, in which year was the tenth of the produce to be given to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow?
a: The third year, the year of the tithe

q: In Deuteronomy 26, what was the Israelite to say he had not done with the sacred portion?
a: Eaten any of it while in mourning

q: But why can our good works not be our righteousness before God, or at least a part of it?
a: God's law requires perfect righteousness; our best works are imperfect and defiled.

q: In Moses' command in Deuteronomy 27, what were the Israelites to coat with plaster and write all the words of the law on after crossing the Jordan?
a: Large stones

q: When Moses told Israel to build an altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal, what were they forbidden to use on the altar's stones?
a: Any iron tool

q: Besides burnt offerings, what kind of offerings were Israel to sacrifice at the altar on Mount Ebal, eating them and rejoicing before the LORD?
a: Peace offerings

q: When Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel in Deuteronomy 27, what did they say the people had become that day?
a: The people of the LORD your God

q: In Deuteronomy 27, the curse on someone who withholds justice names which three groups of people as the ones wronged?
a: The foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow

q: What is required in the first Commandment?
a: To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him

q: How will God bless those who keep His commandments?
a: In this world with peace, favor, guidance, and success; in the next with heaven and eternal glory

q: In Deuteronomy 28, if Israel obeys the LORD, how will their enemies who rise up against them flee?
a: They will flee in seven directions

q: In Deuteronomy 28, what does the LORD say He will open to send rain on Israel's land in season?
a: The heavens, His abundant storehouse

q: In Deuteronomy 28, what does the LORD promise Israel about lending and borrowing if they obey Him?
a: They will lend to many nations but borrow from none

q: Since there is only one God, why do you speak of three persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit?
a: Because God revealed in His Word that these three distinct persons are the one, true God

q: In Deuteronomy 28, what will the sky over disobedient Israel's head and the earth beneath them be like?
a: The sky bronze, and the earth iron

q: In Deuteronomy 28, when Moses warns of defeat for disobedient Israel, in how many directions will they flee from their enemies after marching out against them in one direction?
a: Seven

q: In Deuteronomy 28, what will happen to the foreigner living among disobedient Israel?
a: He will rise higher and higher above them and become the head

q: In Deuteronomy 28:47-48, why will Israel serve the enemies the LORD sends against them?
a: They did not serve the LORD with joy and gladness of heart

q: In Deuteronomy 28, what will the LORD bring against disobedient Israel to swoop down on them like an eagle?
a: A nation from afar whose language they will not understand

q: In Moses' address in Moab, which two kings came out against Israel in battle and were defeated?
a: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan

q: When Moses reviewed the defeat of Sihon and Og, to whom were their lands given as an inheritance?
a: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh

q: Who did Moses say were standing before the LORD in Moab, besides the leaders, elders, officials, men, children and wives, to enter the covenant?
a: The foreigners in their camps who cut wood and draw water

q: Moses said the destruction of the land would be like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and which two other cities?
a: Admah and Zeboiim

q: How many cities did the LORD destroy, with Sodom and Gomorrah among them?
a: Four

q: What were the names of the cities the LORD destroyed in Lot's time?
a: Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim

q: What does God reveal to us through His Law?
a: How we ought to be and what we must do to please God

q: In Deuteronomy 30, if the people return to the LORD after being scattered, what will He do for them even if they were banished to the farthest horizon?
a: He will gather them and return them from there

q: In Deuteronomy 30, to what place does Moses say the LORD will bring the scattered people after they return to Him?
a: The land their fathers possessed

q: In Deuteronomy 30, upon whom will the LORD put all the curses once He has restored His people?
a: Their enemies who hate and persecute them

q: In Moses' final address to Israel in Deuteronomy 30, where does he say the commandment is NOT located, so that no one would need to ask who will go get it?
a: In heaven and beyond the sea

q: In Deuteronomy 30, Moses says the word is very near Israel. Where does he say it is?
a: In your mouth and in your heart

q: What should we do because God promises such rich reward?
a: Love and trust in Him and willingly do according to His commandments.

q: When Moses called heaven and earth as witnesses against Israel, what two pairs did he say he had set before them?
a: Life and death, blessing and cursing

q: When Moses spoke to all Israel in Deuteronomy 31, how old did he say he was?
a: A hundred and twenty years old

q: In Deuteronomy 31, which two kings did Moses say the LORD had destroyed along with their land, as an example of what He would do to the nations ahead?
a: Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites

q: Who is traditionally credited as the author of the book of Deuteronomy?
a: Moses

q: In Moses' command about reading the law to all Israel, during which feast was the law to be read at the end of every seven years?
a: The Feast of Tabernacles

q: In Deuteronomy 31, where did the LORD tell Moses to bring Joshua so that He could commission him?
a: The Tent of Meeting

q: When the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to commission Joshua, in what form did He appear?
a: In a pillar of cloud

q: According to the LORD, what would Israel do after they were in the land flowing with milk and honey and had eaten their fill?
a: Turn to other gods and worship them

q: In Deuteronomy 31, whom did Moses command to take the Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant?
a: The Levites who carried the ark of the covenant

q: When Moses commanded that the elders and officers be assembled, whom did he say he would call to witness against them?
a: Heaven and earth

q: In Deuteronomy 31:30, to whom did Moses recite the words of the song from beginning to end?
a: The whole assembly of Israel
